A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bird-MAE research and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. The supplied v1 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A–F. This allows comparison of newly reported material without assuming the underlying experiments are new.

before.justification: V1 reports original BirdSet classification experiments, pretraining and probing ablations, and few-shot results in Tables 3–7 and Figures 2–4.

after.justification: V2 retains original BirdSet experiments and adds ablations, detailed benchmark results and a preliminary general-audio experiment on AS-20k.

M1.justification: The MAE architecture, cosine-similarity/max-pooling prototype head and frozen-encoder probing are retained. V2 first specifies asymmetric classification loss and equally weighted prototype orthogonality regularization (Section 3.2 and Appendix D). V1 does not specify these losses, so the PDFs cannot establish whether the objective changed or was merely documented.

E1.justification: The eight BirdSet tasks and 1-, 5- and 10-shot scenarios remain. V2 adds actual general-audio evaluation on AudioSet AS-20k in Table 8; previously, broader audio applicability was proposed as future work. Renaming the curated XCL dataset does not establish new domain coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds attentive probing to the few-shot comparison, CLS-token and attentive pooling to the fine-tuning ablation, and BEATs_iter2 to the AS-20k comparison. The principal BirdSet comparator set remains unchanged, including BirdNeXt under revised capitalization.

E3.justification: V2 identifies HSN rather than v1's stated POW as the development dataset and revises the reported curated pretraining size from 1.6M to 1.7M. It adds AUROC and top-1 evaluation and additional experimental controls. Table 5 also revises the attentive probe's reported parameter count from approximately 4.22M to 2.1M; these disclosures do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The original data-curation, training-duration, model-size and probing analyses remain. V2 adds a fixed-backbone domain-pretraining comparison in Figure 3, mixup and alternative-pooling ablations in Table 3, and prototype-count sensitivity for probing and fine-tuning in Table 13.

E5.justification: V1 already reports three-run/subset averages and displays few-shot error bars. V2 identifies those bars as standard deviations, adds numerical uncertainty reporting in Tables 11–12, and explicitly states three random seeds for ablations. An increase in run counts is not established.

E6.justification: V2 substantially expands reported outcomes through general-audio results, additional ablations, attentive few-shot results, and AUROC/top-1 scores. Existing entries also change: BirdNeXt's HSN MAP is 47.12 in v1 versus 45.72 in v2, and Bird-MAE-L's HSN prototypical-probing MAP changes from 49.03 to 49.97. Most principal Bird-MAE fine-tuning scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The cosine-similarity/max-pooling equation and class-specific aggregation retain their mathematical meaning. V2 clarifies notation and supplies standard metric formulas in Appendix B, but adds no substantive theoretical result, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: V2 strengthens the central message by explicitly asserting that domain-specific data alone is insufficient and adaptation of the entire training pipeline is necessary. The Bird-MAE, state-of-the-art BirdSet, prototypical-probing and few-shot benchmark contributions are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting probing effectiveness to pretraining domain and objective, including attentive probing outperforming prototypical probing for Audio-MAE. It acknowledges higher model capacity in comparisons with supervised CNNs and uses preliminary AS-20k evidence to support broader applicability previously discussed only prospectively.

D1.justification: V2 supplies code and checkpoint links where v1 promised future links. Appendices A, C and D newly document sampling caps, few-shot construction, task-specific downstream curation, augmentation probabilities, losses, hyperparameters, search grids and hardware/software. These substantially expand reproducibility information without necessarily establishing implementation changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds NatureLM-audio to bioacoustic research positioning and references on parameter-efficient tuning, SSL benchmarking and mixup, while removing some earlier citations. The overall relationship to general-audio SSL and supervised bird models remains. BirdSet's year/venue revision and duplicate-reference cleanup do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting around whole-pipeline adaptation. Method explanations are reorganized, several sections are renamed, and experimental settings are redistributed between the data section and benchmark sections. This exceeds the presentation changes attributable simply to adding appendices.

P2.justification: V2 converts Table 3 into a three-part display, redraws Figure 3, expands Figure 4 with an attentive curve and revised legend, and adds Figure 5 and Tables 8–13. Existing tables gain columns and revised highlighting, including explicit visual identification of HSN as validation data.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the paper through concrete reproducibility specifications, stronger probing comparisons and additional controlled analyses. However, new reporting inconsistencies limit confidence in the expanded evidence: Audio-MAE's HSN fine-tuning MAP is 44.69% in Table 6 but 0.19 (19%) in Table 11. The improved documentation and comparisons support a modest net gain, tempered by these unresolved conflicts.
